options.option: Keep the heatsink; use the on-die sensors, the IR-drop voltage map, and the thermal camera on the back of the board and on the heatsink, with emissivity tape wherever it looks
options.measures: where the unmetered ~14–17 W goes on the board; current per shire
options.who: us for the host-side readings; AI Foundry's people on site to mount the camera

options.option: A fine thermocouple taped to the heatsink base or fins, never between the lid and the heatsink, read by a standalone logger
options.measures: the heatsink's own temperature, which the camera plan suggests explains the all-ones matmul's 107 s against 162–167 s to 90 °C from the same 80 °C reading (R6, R13; inference); a log independent of the host
options.who: AI Foundry's people on site, with the lab lead's consent; the lab admin powers the host down and up

options.option: A fine thermocouple soldered into a groove cut in the lid's centre (Intel's case-temperature method), on aifoundry1 card 0 during the visit request SH1 already asks for
options.risk: moderate: the lid is cut, and Intel solders the bead in at 150 °C; the heatsink comes off and is re-pasted, which resets that card's fitted thermal constants
options.measures: the lid's temperature at its centre, where Intel defines case temperature; θJC; a physical point between die and cooler
options.who: AI Foundry's people on site, with the lab lead's and AI Foundry's consent for card 0

options.option: A bare card on a bench: 12 V through a relay that a thermocouple at 85 °C opens within half a second, and a fan
options.measures: the bare package's heat capacity and θJA (tests whether the 1.5 s stage is the package)
options.who: whoever holds a spare card, with AI Foundry's consent

options.option: An IR-window liquid cooler on a delidded die, imaged by a mid-wave IR camera as the published setups were (for the P3, a germanium or zinc-selenide window over a mineral-oil film, untried)
options.risk: the card is lost if delidding fails: an exposed die's corners are easily damaged, one slip can damage the parts around it, and a soldered lid needs 165–180 °C to lift
options.cost: thousands of dollars (a 50 mm germanium or zinc-selenide window alone about $900)
options.measures: temperature maps at the scale of a shire
options.who: a lab equipped for delidding and IR imaging, with AI Foundry's consent for the card

options.option: A bare card running short bursts in a lab host
options.measures: nothing: the lid shows one temperature, and bare metal mostly reflects the room

prereq: Options 4 and 5 need a card that may be lost: the loose green board with a copper block on the lab's top shelf, if it is an ET card (unidentified: question 6 in the full camera plan), or card 0 only with AI Foundry's consent.
